_comment: M31 P1 — reachability of every declared R-threshold exit lever against its own leg's TP cap. A lever arming at `arm_r` R cannot fire when arm_r > cap_R = 0.099/(risk/entry). Enforced by scripts/ci/check_lever_reachability.py: the registry `arm_r` must equal config/strategies.yaml, so changing an arm without re-measuring FAILS CI. Design: docs/design/position-telemetry-DESIGN.md. Finding: BL-20260816-TRAIL-DECAY-ARM-R-SITS-ABOVE-THE-VENUE-TP-CAP (PR #9588). THIS FILE RECORDS MEASUREMENTS AND DISPOSITIONS — it changes no behaviour and no value; every arm_r correction is Tier-3 and the operator's.

verdict_legend.reachable: measured; observed cap_R clears arm_r on the large majority of entries
verdict_legend.vol_conditional: measured; SOME entries clear it and some cannot — a real design choice, not a default
verdict_legend.inert: measured; no observed entry could reach the arm
verdict_legend.unmeasured: no entry-conditioned observations yet — NOT 'reachable', and `unmeasured_reason` is required

disposition_legend.ok: the lever is fine as declared
disposition_legend.queued_tier3: a correction is proposed and awaiting the operator; `opened_at` required

basis_note: `order_packages/risk_per_unit` is the AUTHORITATIVE basis — the sized risk the strategy actually used. `entry - stop_loss` is NOT the entry risk (a stop is trailed and amended, and the error has no fixed sign: measured 2026-08-16 the two agreed at 1.00 on gld/qqq, 0.71 on xrp, and 5.66x on one trend_donchian package). `candles/atr` is a cheap unconditional screen and is NOT a bound in either direction — on xrp it overstated reachability 90.5% vs 33.3% because entries are filter-selected.

levers.note: BTC 1h ATR is ~0.333% of price, so cap_R sits far above the arm. The order-package cross-check agrees (16.85R).

live_parity_p80_resweep_2026_08_16.note: NOT an arm-above-cap failure — this is the one leg graded reachable at 100% (cap_R p50 11.91 vs arm 6.49). The live-parity sweep proposes a LOWER arm (5.5) and that cell then fails OOS, which is a different question: whether the lever earns its place on this leg at all.

levers.unmeasured_reason: No entry-conditioned pull yet. The candle screen reads cap_R p50 3.56 vs arm 5.57 (2.8% reach), which points at near-inert — but the candle basis overstated xrp by 2.7x and is not a bound, so this is NOT recorded as a verdict.
levers.note: Needs its own order-packages pull (one path per relay issue — six paths share one 55KB budget and starved every leg to 1-3 rows).

live_parity_p80_resweep_2026_08_16.note: Proposes 1.5R — far below the declared 5.57 — and still fails OOS. The candle screen had pointed at near-inert; this neither confirms nor refutes reachability, it says the cell does not clear the gate at any arm it proposes.

levers.note: THE DECIDABLE ONE. Not one entry in the leg's entire life could have reached its own declared arm; risk/entry ran 3.294-4.506% against the 1.956% the arm needs. atr_stop_mult is 2.0 here, not 2.5. Either re-sweep the arm at live parity and take the corrected value, or record the lever as inert so the coverage matrix stops counting it as shipped — Tier-3, operator's call.

live_parity_p80_resweep_2026_08_16.note: ⚠️ THE PROPOSED ARM IS ITSELF UNREACHABLE ON THIS LEG'S OWN ENTRIES — DO NOT SHIP 3.86. It needs risk/entry <= 2.565%; the 8 live entries (a COMPLETE history) ran 3.294-4.506%, giving cap_R 2.20-3.01. 3.86 exceeds the best observed cap_R by 0.85R, so zero of 8 could arm it. Taking this PASS at face value would replace one inert arm with a SECOND inert arm carrying a pass badge — worse, because the badge suppresses the next question. NOT RESOLVED HERE: the p80 is over backtest winner MFEs (134 lifetime trades) while cap_R is over 8 live order packages; either the live entries are unrepresentative or the backtest risk/entry differs systematically. Both testable, neither tested.

levers.basis: order_packages/risk_per_unit — TRUNCATED (55,429 of 224,462 bytes: the 6 NEWEST of up to 25)
levers.note: Neither inert nor reachable: 4 of the 6 newest entries could not have armed it. Do NOT read 33.3% as a lifetime rate — the sample is truncated and recency-biased. The live 18-day short (trade 4163) sits at cap_R 3.92, i.e. in the unreachable part of the distribution, which is why its trail ran at base mult the whole time. The candle screen said 90.5% and was wrong.

live_parity_p80_resweep_2026_08_16.note: The proposed 2.17R WOULD be reachable (observed cap_R 3.92-8.38) and the cell STILL fails OOS — so 'lower the arm' is not the answer on this leg either. That closes the escape the gld row leaves open.

levers.note: THIN (n=1 entry-conditioned) but the two independent bases agree exactly at cap_R 2.13 against arm 3.56. Capped via builder_unit:trend_donchian, not by family string — a family-only test under-claimed here.

live_parity_p80_resweep_2026_08_16.note: SKIPPED, not failed: 21 winner MFEs against a 30 minimum. The harness DECLINED to emit a p80 rather than producing one off a thin sample. Absence of evidence — this leg remains exactly as measured before (inert, n=1).

levers.unmeasured_reason: No entry-conditioned pull yet. The candle screen reads cap_R p50 2.22 vs arm 2.00 (73.6% reach) — the arm sits just below the median ceiling, so this is the leg most sensitive to which basis is used and least safe to grade off the screen.

live_parity_p80_resweep_2026_08_16.note: SKIPPED, not failed: 14 winner MFEs against a 30 minimum. Still unmeasured; the re-sweep could not resolve it.

levers.unmeasured_reason: Not yet measured, but the arm needs only risk/entry <= 9.9% to be reachable — a threshold no plausible 1h ATR approaches, so this is recorded as unmeasured rather than parked as a risk.
levers.note: Capped via builder_unit:trend_donchian. Disposition 'ok' is permitted because the verdict is `unmeasured`, not `inert`/`vol_conditional`; the guard requires an explicit disposition only for the two measured-bad verdicts.

levers.basis: order_packages/risk_per_unit — TRUNCATED (6 newest of up to 25; relay #9624)
levers.note: Measured BECAUSE this guard demanded it: PR #9549 declares this arm on a real-money leg (bybit_2) and had no reachability record, so the guard would have failed it — the first live catch, within the hour. The measurement SUPPORTS the PR: 5 of 6 recent entries clear arm 2.0, risk/entry 2.416-5.021%. The one miss is marginal (risk/entry 5.021% -> cap_R 1.97 vs arm 2.00), so a high-vol entry can still land just under the arm; that is a real characteristic of the leg, not a defect, and it is why the verdict is `reachable` rather than a claim that it always arms. Sample is truncated and recency-biased (55KB relay budget) — not a lifetime rate. Entry added ahead of #9549 merging so the two PRs are mergeable in either order.

_resweep_note: config/lever_reachability.json records REACHABILITY (can a declared arm fire under its own TP cap). The live_parity_p80_resweep_2026_08_16 block on each entry records a SEPARATE question answered on 2026-08-16: what arm a live-parity p80 sweep proposes, and whether that cell clears its gate. THE TWO CAN DISAGREE, and on gld_pullback_1d they do — the sweep's PASSING arm (3.86) is itself above that leg's measured cap_R (2.20-3.01). Read both before proposing any arm value. No arm_r was changed; every correction remains Tier-3 and the operator's.
